The figure above shows the graph of a piecewise linear function $y=f(x).$ The point $A$ has coordinates $(1,0)$ and lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $(0,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ what is $({f}^{-1})^{′}(0)?$
worked_solution:
Since $(0,1)$ lies on ${f}^{-1},$ we have ${f}^{-1}(0)=1.$ 
The slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ for $x\in [0,2]$ is $-2$, hence, ${f}^{′}(1)=-2.$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse function is 

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(0) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(0))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
